model.title: Ossoff's stated reluctance trims his Democratic odds; broader outlook holds
model.summary: The model modestly reduces Jon Ossoff’s nomination chance because he says he is not running, while his recent polling strength limits the size of the change; the difference moves to Other. No new general-election polls warrant changes to the national or state outlook, and Nikki Haley’s zero-probability entry is removed because she has ruled out a 2028 bid.

overview.summary:
Democrats are favoured to win the 2028 presidential election, but the edge is modest and the race is far from settled. Democrats won the 2026 national House vote by more than 13 points and made broad statewide gains, including in Texas and Georgia. Hypothetical national polls for 2028 show no clear lead for either side, so the advantage rests mainly on the broader political environment rather than on head-to-head polling.

Presidential approval stood at about -26 net in late November, down from earlier in the fall, which weighs against the incumbent party. October unemployment was 4.1% after 165,000 jobs were added, but reports of persistent inflation keep economic sentiment mixed. Arizona, North Carolina, Nevada, Georgia, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin and Michigan are the states where the contest is closest, and most of them will decide the outcome.
overview.watch: The first Democratic primary debate, scheduled for June 2027, and any declared candidacies from Buttigieg, Ocasio-Cortez or Shapiro could shift both the nomination picture and the national outlook.
key_factors: Democrats won the 2026 national House vote by more than 13 points, a result that points toward a favourable environment for their party in 2028.
Presidential net approval was about -26 in late November and has declined since early November.
Unemployment was 4.1% in October, with 165,000 jobs added, while persistent inflation keeps economic views mixed.
Hypothetical national matchups show no clear advantage for either party, leaving the outcome sensitive to the closest battleground states.

nominations.D: The Democratic primary remains wide open, with Kamala Harris, Gavin Newsom, Pete Buttigieg and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez among the leading contenders and no clear frontrunner in primary polling.
nominations.R: Marco Rubio and JD Vance are near the front of a fluid Republican field, with Rubio gaining support among House Republicans, Vance saying he will decide next year, and Ron DeSantis keeping the door open to a run.

storylines.title: Democrats post a sweeping 2026 midterm result
storylines.detail: Democrats won the national House vote by 13.31 points and made broad statewide gains, including strong results in Texas and Georgia. Florida was a Republican outlier relative to the national House result, and the forecast retains its limited Florida-specific adjustment.

storylines.title: Approval and economic signals point in different directions
storylines.detail: Presidential net approval was -25.7 on November 24, down from -23.7 on November 1. October unemployment was 4.1% after 165,000 jobs were added, while the economic index remains unavailable amid reports of persistent inflation.

storylines.title: The Democratic primary remains wide open
storylines.detail: Polling shows a varied field, with Harris, Newsom, Buttigieg and Ocasio-Cortez among the leading contenders. Ossoff’s recent polling is strong, but he says he is not running, so the forecast has reduced his odds and retains substantial probability on Other.

storylines.title: Shapiro's reelection and groundwork strengthen his case
storylines.detail: Shapiro's reelection, large margin, federal PAC and recent comments about his ambitions keep him in the 2028 conversation; November coverage describes him as set to run. Primary polling remains modest, so the forecast gives him only a small nomination probability.

storylines.title: Rubio gains ground in a fluid GOP contest
storylines.detail: Primary polling places Rubio and Vance near the front of the field, and recent reporting describes stronger support for Rubio among House Republicans. Vance says he will decide next year, while DeSantis has kept the door open to a run.

storylines.title: AOC's team activity and new backing add to 2028 signals
storylines.detail: A progressive group, New York socialists and Rep.-elect Brad Lander have backed a potential Ocasio-Cortez bid, and reporting describes team activity as she weighs a 2028 decision. These signals stop short of a declared campaign, so the forecast keeps her nomination odds near their prior level.

storylines.title: Democrats plan 12 primary debates beginning in June 2027
storylines.detail: The DNC has announced plans for 12 debates in the 2028 cycle, with the first scheduled for June 2027, and has adopted rules requiring candidates to reject super PAC and dark-money spending. Michigan will host one debate, adding an organizing milestone without distinguishing among potential nominees.

storylines.title: Buttigieg allies organize around a possible 2028 bid
storylines.detail: A new PAC launched by Buttigieg supporters is seeking to recruit him for another presidential run. It is a concrete organizing signal, though Buttigieg has not declared a campaign and the primary remains unsettled.

revisions.title: Whitmer's reported decision removes her from the Democratic field
revisions.summary: The model removes Gretchen Whitmer from the Democratic nominee list after November 23 coverage reported that she would not run, transferring her small probability to Other. No new general-election polls or other evidence warrants changes to the broader forecast.

revisions.title: New Republican backing gives Rubio a small nomination-odds boost
revisions.summary: The model modestly raises Marco Rubio’s Republican nomination chance after November 25 reporting described stronger support for him among House Republicans, drawing the increase from Other. It removes Nikki Haley’s zero-probability entry after her decision to skip the race; with no new general-election polls, the broader forecast remains unchanged.

revisions.title: Shapiro's firmer run signal modestly lifts his Democratic odds
revisions.summary: The model slightly raises Josh Shapiro’s nomination chance after new coverage describes him as set to run, with the increase coming from Other. It also updates Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s general-election effect to match the polling-strength regression and keeps the broader outlook unchanged with no new general-election polls.

revisions.title: Shapiro's clearer 2028 signals modestly lift his Democratic odds
revisions.summary: The model slightly raises Josh Shapiro’s Democratic nomination chance after new coverage describes him as preparing for a 2028 run, offsetting the increase from Other. It removes Nikki Haley, who has ruled out a bid; with no new general-election polls, the broader outlook remains unchanged.

revisions.title: Fresh Rubio support nudges his GOP nomination odds higher
revisions.summary: The model modestly raises Marco Rubio’s Republican nomination chance after a November 25 report described stronger support for him among House Republicans, with the increase coming from Other. General-election settings and the rest of the candidate field hold, while Nikki Haley’s zero-probability entry is removed because she has ruled out a run.
